events.text:
Step 1 of 4: Setup

Here is how this works:

```
You give:  your resume, the job posting, a few sentences in your own words
   ↓
I write a draft, from your facts only
   ↓
A second AI, from a different company, checks it without knowing who wrote it
   ↓
Automatic checks, then you approve every changed line
   ↓
Your resume, the job requirements it does not show, and likely interview questions
```

It runs by itself; you answer a few questions along the way. A second AI checks the work because an AI tends to go easy on its own writing.

**What I read from your resume**
- Biology Teacher, Public High School, Aug 2019 to Present
- Student Teacher, Public Middle School, Jan 2019 to May 2019
- M.Ed. Curriculum and Instruction (2022), B.S. Biology (2018), Certificate in Instructional Design (2026), NC Professional Educator License, Biology 9-12

The posting gives no level, so I assumed an entry to mid level Instructional Designer role in the United States (Charlotte, NC, hybrid). Tell me if that's wrong.

**One question:** the posting asks for a portfolio, and you mention a Rise course you built for yours. Do you have a link to it, or to LinkedIn or any other page about your work? Most recruiters look for LinkedIn. If not, that's fine.

**My plan**
1. Quick review: I write the draft and one second AI checks it, about 6 minutes in all, one call to it. The other choice is a full council, where three AIs each draft and check each other's work (about 15 minutes and about five times the AI usage). The only other AI I found that could join a council offers just its fast model here, so I recommend the quick review.
2. No extra research on the role (the posting is detailed), I polish the final wording, and you get a plain-text copy while we work. A PDF needs a tool that isn't installed on this computer, so the final copy will be plain text (Markdown) unless you'd like me to set that up.

**Before anything is sent:** I've hidden your name and contact details. They come back at the end. The second AI will be OpenAI's Codex, running GPT-6 Astra. (A full council would also use Google's Antigravity, running Gemini 3.8 Flash High.) The working files are in `.tribunal/` inside your folder. This text, including your employers, job history and the pages your links point to, will go to OpenAI's Codex under its terms and your account settings there. Some keep their own history, and the text can still identify you. Leave out anything confidential to an employer, and check whether this employer allows AI help with applications.

Answer the question, or say "yes" to take the defaults and go ahead.
Quick review, please. Yes to the defaults, go ahead. No other links.
Draft

Step 2 of 4: Draft

Thanks. Quick review it is. I'm writing the draft from your resume and your own words now.

Step 3 of 4: Review and sign-off

The second AI read the draft as a hiring manager. It found no line that claims more than you told me. It would not phone yet, mainly because the posting asks for Storyline and you haven't used it; it read the resume as entry level. I took its suggestions that fit your facts, and the draft is at `.tribunal/resume.md`.

**Changes I made that don't change any fact**
- New summary, from your own words: seven years teaching, your M.Ed. and certificate, Canvas, the Camtasia videos and the lab safety workshop.
- Moved the lab safety workshop near the top of your teaching role, since it is your clearest training for adults.
- Rewrote your teaching bullets from your own words (Canvas courses, about 60 Camtasia videos, the AP review change and pass rate, the cells unit) and added the hand hygiene module as a project.
- Wrote "Articulate Rise" as "Articulate Rise 360", the posting's name for the same tool, and put all dates in one style.
- Cut "classroom management", "Developed engaging lesson plans aligned with state standards" and the Science Olympiad club, to keep the page on design work. The curriculum committee and Canvas grading lines are folded into the cells unit and Canvas bullets.
- Storyline stays off, since you said you've only watched demos.

**Questions, only about facts**
1. Your old resume lists **lesson planning, differentiated instruction and Google Workspace**. Nothing newer mentions them. Are they still true and current?
2. The hand hygiene module is dated **2026**. Did you build it in 2026?
3. For the AP Biology pass rate, what counts as a pass (for example, a score of 3 or higher on the AP exam)?
4. If you know them: who the module was written for, its learning objective, and how it checks what learners learned. Leave this out if you're not sure.
5. Would you like the schools named? Right now they read "Public High School" and "Public Middle School".

Are all of these true, and could you explain each in an interview? Tell me any to fix. If you don't know a number, I'll leave it out, so please don't estimate.

One small layout warning remains: the skills line wraps by a few words.

Answer the questions above, or say "all true" if everything is right as it is.

1. Lesson planning and Google Workspace, yes, I use both every week. Differentiated instruction, I'd rather leave that off.
2. Yes, I built it in spring 2026.
3. A pass is a 3 or higher on the AP exam. The numbers come from the College Board report for our school. I don't know how many students took it each year.
4. I'm not sure enough to say, so leave it out.
5. Keep them as "Public High School" and "Public Middle School", no names.

Finalise

Step 4 of 4: Finalise

Thanks. I worked your answers in:
- Lesson planning and Google Workspace stay; differentiated instruction is off.
- The AP Biology bullet now says a pass means a 3 or higher.
- The module's audience, objective and assessment stay off, and the schools stay unnamed.

Your resume, with your name and contact details back in, is at `.tribunal/final.md`. It passes the automatic checks with no errors and is about 280 words, well within one page. The only warnings left are about "Articulate Rise", which your own words back (the Rise course you built), so I left them.

Want one more blind look before it's final? About a minute.

Is it final? Say "it's final", or tell me what to change.
No thanks. Yes, it's final. Markdown is fine.
Final check: 0 errors, 2 warnings (Articulate Rise, backed by her own words), 285 words

Step 4 of 4: Finalise

Done. Your resume is at `.tribunal/final.md`, as a plain-text copy (Markdown). To use it, paste it into Word or Google Docs and apply heading styles. The final check passed with no errors.

**What the posting asks for that the resume does not show**
- Articulate Storyline 360 (you've only watched demos)
- Cornerstone, or any LMS other than Canvas
- Accessibility to WCAG 2.1 AA
- Measuring training with the Kirkpatrick model in practice (you learned it in the certificate)
- Working with subject matter experts such as nurse educators, pharmacists or compliance staff (the nurse who checked your module and the teachers on the cells unit are the closest)
- Job aids
- A portfolio link, which the posting asks for
- A healthcare background (your science background is shown)

**Questions an interviewer is likely to ask**
1. What did you build yourself in the hand hygiene module, and what did the nurse say about it? (Tests how well you know Rise and whether the review happened.)
2. What else changed between your 2022 and 2025 AP Biology classes? (Tests how much of the pass rate you can put down to the weekly practice questions. If asked how many students took the exam, it's fine to say you don't know.)
3. For the lab safety workshop, what did you design, what did you deliver, and how did you check that the teachers learned it? (Tests what "ran" covered.)
4. What was your own part in rewriting the cells unit? Walk through one objective, its lesson and its quiz item. (Tests your share of team work and how you line up objectives with assessment.)
5. Where did you use ADDIE in your module, and what would a Kirkpatrick evaluation of it measure? (Tests whether the coursework turns into real design decisions.)

Save what you told me (your resume, your own words and the facts you confirmed) on this computer, so your next job needs fewer questions? It stays in `~/.resume-tribunal/`, goes nowhere else, and you can delete the folder any time. I can also delete the working files in `.tribunal/` if you'd like.
No thanks.
